name: Jengu
body:
JENGU
CR 6

A water spirit with long flowing hair, its form blending human beauty with a shimmering fish-like lower body.

XP 2,400
CG Medium fey (aquatic, shapechanger)
Init +8; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +14

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 15, flat-footed 14 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +4 natural)
hp 76 (9d6+45)
Fort +7, Ref +10, Will +8
DR 5/cold iron; Resist cold 20

OFFENSE

Speed 10 ft., swim 60 ft.
Melee jengu staff +9 (1d8+1/×3)
Special Attacks fatebending
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 7th; concentration +10)

At Will—alter self (self only, matching their human upper half), create water, dancing lights, detect magic, guidance, prestidigitation, purify food and drink, stabilize
5/day—cure moderate wounds, detect thoughts (DC 15), faerie fire, hydraulic push, obscuring mist, protection from evil
3/day—control water, dispel magic, remove disease, summon nature’s ally III, water breathing
1/day—summon nature’s ally IV

STATISTICS

Str 11, Dex 18, Con 18, Int 13, Wis 14, Cha 17
Base Atk +4; CMB +4; CMD 24 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Defensive Combat Training, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Toughness, Weapon Finesse
Skills Acrobatics +16 (+8 when jumping), Diplomacy +15, Knowledge (nature) +13, Perception +14, Sense Motive +14, Stealth +16, Swim +20; Racial Modifiers +8 Acrobatics when jumping
Languages Aquan, Common, Sylvan
SQ amphibious
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks swallow whole (1d6 bludgeoning damage, AC 11, 15 hp)

STATISTICS

Str 19, Dex 16, Con 16, Int 7, Wis 8, Cha 7
Base Atk +3; CMB +8 (+12 to grab); CMD 20
Feats Improved Natural Attack (bite), Lightning Reflexes, Run
Skills Acrobatics +7, Intimidate +1, Perception +9, Stealth +10, Survival +1; Racial Modifiers +4 Perception, +4 Stealth
Languages Abyssal, Common

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Curse of Destruction (Su)

The jengu curses a target object within 120 feet to break, malfunction, or otherwise fail. If magical or in a creature’s possession, the item must succeed at a DC 17 Fortitude save. Unattended non-magical items receive no saving throw. Damage that the object takes ignores hardness, and the item counts as having the broken condition. Unless the curse is removed, the object breaks in a manner determined by the GM sometime before sunset the next day. Once an object is targeted by this ability, it cannot be targeted by it again for the next 24 hours. This is a curse effect. The save DC is Charismabased.

Fatebending (Su)

As an immediate action, a jengu can bends fate to help or hinder a target creature within 120 feet.

When the target is about to make a d20 roll, the target must the roll twice and take the better result if the jengu chooses fortune or the worse result if the jengu chooses misfortune.

Jengu Staff (Su)

This simple driftwood staff functions as a +1 elven branched spearmtt, but only for a jengu.

Stalwart defenders of nature, these mermaid-like water sprits can be found in oceans, rivers, and lakes. Those who honor the Jengu are said to receive great fortune. Jengu have beautiful humanoid upper bodies, while their lower bodies are adapted to their chosen aquatic habitat. They act as guides to animals and those who respect nature, but they vigorously assault any who disrespect their natural habitats. Jengu rarely fend for themselves, unless they live in extremely remote areas, as locals often leave offerings of food, drink, and trinkets to earn boons. Many village priests directly engage with Jengu to foster a symbiotic relationship in which the people provide sustenance and gifts in exchange for favors or defense. Many Jengu act as patrons to local populations, and festivals are held to honor them.

Jengu avoid direct combat, preferring to use their relationships with animals and humanoids as support. When pressed, they may use a staff made of driftwood, coupled with their fate bending power, to drive off foes. Jengu use stealth and their fate bending to sabotage people and objects they fear will pollute or despoil the waters of their protected territory.

ECOLOGY

Environment any water
Organization solitary, pair, or shoal (3–6)
Treasure standard (jengu staff, other treasure)
